text: Using qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, we tested a label-dropout scheme that randomly drops a fraction of weak labels each epoch, with label_dropout set to 0.1. Across num_seeds = 10, the weak supervisor reached 0.63 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.88, while the strong student trained on weak labels attained a transfer accuracy of 0.83 with a standard error of 0.03. The resulting performance gap recovered was 0.79 with a standard error of 0.12, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.45; the margin exceeds twice the reported standard error, so the method appears to improve recovery relative to the baseline under this setup. Caveats: the PGR standard error of 0.12 is sizeable, no standard error is reported for the baseline PGR, and the finding rests on a single model pair and one dropout setting, so generalization is untested.
